# openbim-ifc-py

Python bindings for openbim-ifc: read, edit and write IFC STEP files from Python.

## Overview

Python bindings for the IFC facade (ADR 0013, #39).

The compiled module is `openbim_ifc._native`; the public API is the pure
Python package `openbim_ifc`, which wraps it and defines the value
classes. Values cross as plain dicts in the tagged encoding shared with
the WASM and C bindings; `openbim_ifc` turns them into frozen dataclasses.

This crate adds calling-convention glue only. IFC behaviour belongs in
`openbim-ifc`, shared binding behaviour in `openbim-ifc-binding-core`.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.16.0 (2026-11-09):

### Changed (wire format 1.5)

- The geometry graph payload (#367) may be Axiolid's wire format 1.5, written only when a graph holds a ruled surface (axiolid/kernel#402); every other graph keeps its version. The newest version the build advertises (`GEOMETRY_FORMAT_VERSION`) is `"1.5"`. A reader on `axiolid-model` 0.3.17 or older refuses `1.5`.

### Added (#603)

- `SurfaceColour.source` can be `"materialSet"`: `source_entity` is the set (`IfcMaterialLayerSet`, `IfcMaterialProfileSet`, `IfcMaterialConstituentSet` or `IfcMaterialList`, or a usage of one (`IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage`, `IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage` and its `Tapering`)) whose materials all state the colour, and the new `source_materials` (a tuple, last field) lists the materials of the set that colour the item: every one, or the constituents its shape aspects name (ascending id, distinct); `()` for other sources.

Semver: minor (pre-1.0 breaking: a record field is added).

### Changed (#651)

- `representation` accepts `"Reference"`, the void geometry of an IFC4 Reference View opening.

Semver: patch (additive).

### Changed (#614)

- A diagnostic string with a position reads "warning at line L, column C
  (bytes a..b): ...".

Semver: patch (Display text changes)

### Fixed (#617)

- The first id handed out after a read is above every declared and
  referenced id, so a new entity never takes the id of a dangling reference
  or a skipped record.

Semver: patch
